line: A firefly's blink is a question: a girl gets her answer as a deer, loses every light in a storm, and asks the whole dark with the last one.
line_cn: 萤火虫闪一下就是在发问：女孩得到的回答是一只鹿，暴风雨吹灭了所有的光，她用最后一只问遍了整片黑夜。

camera.serves: a walk, a ride, time passing
a crowd revealed across the whole horizon

camera.expresses: a change of place without a cut
camera.serves: travel, time jumps, a final tableau

transitions: Transitions happen only inside the medium: a flow pours in, a swirl gathers, a gust blows the scene away and it re-forms elsewhere, lights go out, the world re-forms upward.
No hard cuts, dissolves or page turns.
labels: Titles and credits are made of points: the text is rendered to a mask and sampled on a jittered grid (not randomly), one particle per sample. A 140–170 px CJK title needs about 3,400 points, a 30–40 px Latin line about 800; sparser and the strokes stop reading. Once landed, the text holds absolutely still (sub-pixel shimmer only), with a short flash on landing. Place it in empty sky, left-aligned, never centred over a character, never on a plate.

Subtitles are plain type burned in (legibility first), a soft brush-like CJK face such as LXGW WenKai (OFL): Chinese ≈ 40 px in warm cream, English ≈ 28 px a little dimmer, centred at the bottom, no outline, no plate, only a faint glow of the same colour. Keep every subject above the subtitle band.
motion: 60 fps, every frame (no stepping). Particle paths are always curves: straight flight gets a rotation or scatter added.

Breathing: character points pulse slowly (± 22 %), and a few points are much brighter than the rest (pointillist sparkle). Fireflies are mostly dark: a narrow pulse, so only about a quarter are lit at any moment.
Drift instead of physics: a sum of slow sines (0.3–1.4 rad/s) for floating points; easing replaces damping (ease-out to land, smootherstep elsewhere).

Performance: big silhouette actions only (look up, reach, lower the head, jump, run, fall, kneel, stand, raise an arm). Blinks and fingers cannot be drawn. A large figure keeps its full silhouette while it acts: when it bows or leaps, move the head, neck and legs and keep the back line and every limb readable.

native_moves.name: The pour-in
native_moves.does: a stream of light enters from off-frame and lands, point by point, as the world and its characters.

native_moves.name: The guiding light
native_moves.does: the single brightest point in the film (strong halo) leads the eye and can become a character's eye.

native_moves.name: Synchronous flash
native_moves.does: a ripple delayed by distance (1 + 2.6·exp(−((t − t0 − d/v)/0.08)²)), or the whole field at once. For: an answer, a connection, "the world heard".

native_moves.name: Swirl gathering
native_moves.does: points rotate around the new form's centre while they fly and focus. For: a summoning, a birth, many becoming one; the same move scales from a life-size animal to one taller than the frame.

native_moves.name: Gust change of scene
native_moves.does: delay by screen x (one side leaves first), a wind vector, scatter; streaks come from motion blur. Wind direction is story direction (following wind = travel, head wind = storm).

native_moves.name: Going out
native_moves.does: blown apart and not re-formed, brightness down to 1–2 %, embers left on the ground. For: loss.

native_moves.name: Identity swap
native_moves.does: the same points change role without a break in the picture (a sun → a clock face, sparks → a flock of birds → the title).

native_moves.name: Arc jump
native_moves.does: one rig's points fly from one pose and place to another (a leap across a gap, a dive); a facing flip can hide inside it.

native_moves.name: Into a constellation
native_moves.does: a whole character leaps with its rig intact, shrinks, turns sharp and cool, and keeps walking in the sky as stars.

score.note: harp glissandi, glockenspiel and chimes for single lights, flute melody
